v: Twenty-two years later, Tara Singh made me forget logic, changed sensibilities and all my grown-up perspectives — pure nostalgia, goosebumps and Sunny Deol mass magic 🙏😇
e: I entered GADAR 2 worried that my changed sensibilities might ruin the affection I still had for the 2001 original. Within 15 minutes, the nostalgia took over. Once Tara Singh enters Pakistan, logic disappears, the goosebumps return and Sunny Deol reminds you exactly why this character became iconic.
body:
Back in 2001, I had just stepped into Intermediate First Year. This was much, much before the social-media era, and there was unusual euphoria in Guntur around a couple of newly released Hindi films — at a time when even getting a direct Hindi release in town was relatively rare.

As a teenager with limited understanding of the world and still building my own perspectives, I absolutely loved the innocence of Tara Singh and the love story between him and his Madam Ji!!!!

Then came the second half... and I got full goosebumps watching Tara Singh bash Pakistani goons and army men with his bare hands — with a little assistance from that iconic hand pump 😇

Cut to 22 years later.

When GADAR 2 was announced, I was genuinely sceptical about how I would react to it. My sensibilities had changed, my perspective on borders and people had changed, and I was worried that the sequel might now look cringe to me — or worse, somehow damage the affection I still had for GADAR.

So I stepped into the theatre with all those doubts and with a fairly good idea of what the story would be.

BUT... BUT... BUT...

Within 10–15 minutes, I forgot almost all my perspectives, sensibilities and logic and got completely sucked into the movie 😂

I actually became restless waiting for Tara Singh to enter Pakistan. And once he does... the familiar goosebumps return.

I thoroughly enjoyed the way the director plays with nostalgia, bringing back glimpses and memories from the first GADAR at exactly the moments designed to trigger old fans.

And YES — the iconic hand pump makes a comeback too... but this time with dignity 🤣

More than anything, GADAR 2 feels like a tribute to Sunny Deol.

He has had a long series of forgettable films over the years, and he may very well have more of them in future 😜 But Tara Singh reminds you what Sunny Deol is capable of when the character, dialogue and mass emotion align perfectly with his personality 🙏

The two iconic songs — Ghar Aaja Pardesi and Main Nikla Gaddi Leke — are retained, and they still carry almost the same magic they did 22 years ago 🙏🙏

If you watched GADAR back in 2001 and have memories attached to that era, GADAR 2 is a must-watch because it becomes a wonderful nostalgia trip into the period when massy patriotic Hindi films had their own unique theatrical flavour.

If you are a much younger viewer with no emotional connection to the original, though, you may want to keep your expectations in check. This filmmaking style belongs proudly to another era — and that is simultaneously its biggest strength and its biggest limitation.

v: Don’t let regular reviews fool you — this Meher Ramesh remake is still better than the legendary Aacharyaaa 💪😂 That is also almost the nicest thing I can say about it.
e: BHOLA SHANKAR feels less like a movie and more like a చిరు ఉపాధి పధకం for people desperate to work with Chiranjeevi. The outdated remake, weak music, cringe comedy and wasted Vedalam moments convinced me that Chiru urgently needs fresher directors and content rather than another fan-driven project.
body:
Don’t let the regular reviews fool you — Meher Ramesh’s remake is still better than Koratala Siva’s original masterpiece Aacharyaaa 💪😂

And that is probably the nicest thing I can say about BHOLA SHANKAR.

This doesn’t feel like a movie as much as a చిరు ఉపాధి పధకం — an employment scheme for people who desperately wanted to be part of a Chiranjeevi film 🙏

I strongly believe Chiru should stop entertaining so-called fans by automatically giving them opportunities in acting, direction or other departments simply because they belong to the bhajana batch.

This movie is a perfect example of how weak the final product can become when admiration for the star starts replacing honest creative collaboration.

Whatever the quality of a Chiranjeevi film, one thing that traditionally rarely disappoints is the music.

Well... thanks to Mahati Swara Sagar, BHOLA SHANKAR manages to disappoint me there too 😞

At times it feels as if the producers and Chiru himself wanted to put together a quick remake using an already outdated story, assuming familiarity and star power would do most of the work.

The project then seems to have attracted actors and technicians eager simply for the opportunity to say they worked with Megastar — which again brings me back to my చిరు ఉపాధి పధకం theory 😂

When this movie was announced, everybody was naturally sceptical. Still, I had one small hope: Vedalam had a couple of stylish, high-octane sequences that actually looked suitable for Meher Ramesh’s flashy filmmaking style.

Unfortunately, he manages to mess up even those opportunities.

I have always been a huge fan of Chiru’s comedy timing, but here the comedy felt cringe to the core.

The attempt to make Chiranjeevi imitate Pawan Kalyan looks artificial rather than affectionate, and the recreation of the famous nadumu scene from Kushi turns something cute and romantic in the original into something painfully awkward 🙄

It is high time Chiranjeevi works with new-age directors and newer content — even darker or more unusual subjects if needed — rather than repeatedly falling back on remakes that offer audiences almost nothing new.

More importantly, he should work with filmmakers who are confident enough to challenge him creatively, not people whose fandom automatically gives the star complete control over the content 😢

PS: Pawan Kalyan sudden ga women trafficking gurinchi maatladinappude telusukovalsindi... BHOLA SHANKAR promotions chesthunnadani 😉

v: After a long time, a proper treat for Thalaivar fans — half-cooked story maybe, but Rajini’s swag + killer cameos + Anirudh BGM make it a far better Rajini outing than his recent run 🙏
e: JAILER is average-to-good as a film, but Nelson succeeds at something many recent directors struggled with: balancing Rajinikanth’s larger-than-life style with enough story to hold the movie together. The cameos and Anirudh’s terrific BGM provide most of the extra theatrical lift.
body:
After a long time... this is a proper treat for Thalaivar fans!!!!

Nelson achieves something many new-age directors have struggled with: finding a reasonable balance between Rajinikanth’s style and a story without allowing the superstar treatment to completely swallow the movie.

Content-wise, the story is somewhere between half-cooked and decent and follows a structure that occasionally reminded me of the Vikram format, including its twists and extended-universe-style cameos.

But for a neutral viewer, what really holds the film together is Rajini’s swag.

Add the appearances by Shiva Rajkumar, Mohanlal and Jackie Shroff, then let Anirudh blast those moments with his terrific BGM... and suddenly even fairly ordinary material becomes a proper theatrical event.

Overall, JAILER is an Average-to-Good movie for me.

It definitely could have been better as a complete film, but it is still a far, far, far better Rajinikanth movie than most of what I had seen from him in the immediate years before this 🙏

t: Adipurush — My Take on the Reactions 😉
v: Adipurush was badly made — but I still don’t buy the grand political conspiracy theories from either side. Sometimes a badly executed movie is simply... a badly executed movie 😉
e: Five days after Adipurush released, I found the competing political theories around its failure more baffling than the film itself. My take was simpler: Ramayana deserved a modern retelling, the producer-director-star choices were understandable on paper, but the CGI, adaptation choices and execution went badly wrong.
body:
It had been almost five days since Adipurush released and, no doubt, I thought it was a badly made film.

But some of the grand theories being circulated online about why the movie was made — and who was supposedly behind it — baffled me even more than the movie itself 🤷🏻‍♂️

Opinion 1: “This was a political project built around Shri Ram sentiment.”

One side argued that a political party had effectively backed or taken ownership of the movie so that religious sentiment could be converted into money and political benefit.

My counter: I genuinely wondered whether people making that claim had watched the final product 😂 If an organised political machinery had carefully designed a religious propaganda film, I would at least expect the execution to be competent enough not to irritate even deeply religious viewers.

The final film, for me, was too badly handled to support the idea of some brilliantly coordinated political master plan.

Opinion 2: “This was an anti-Hindu Bollywood conspiracy.”

The opposite camp argued that Bollywood and political liberals had deliberately tried to damage Ramayana and portray Hindu culture badly.

My counter: I found that theory equally unconvincing. In the political climate of the time, deliberately spending enormous money on a nationally visible Ramayana adaptation purely to offend a massive audience would be an extraordinary commercial and political risk.

So what do I think actually happened?

Let’s start with the official producer, T-Series.

If we rewind to our childhood in the early and mid-1990s, many of us remember Gulshan Kumar and T-Series being strongly associated with devotional songs and religious content covering Hindu gods and goddesses.

So T-Series participating in a major Ramayana project never seemed strange to me, nor did I need a party-political explanation for it.

Also, if we look at Indian television and movie history, every generation or two has retold epics like Ramayana and Mahabharata using the storytelling styles and technology available at that time.

We have seen multiple television versions of Mahabharata — some hugely popular, some average and some forgettable.

But after the famous older Ramayana adaptations and the animated version many of us grew up with, a large-scale modern cinematic retelling of Ramayana had been due for a long time.

Maybe the cultural moment around the Ram Mandir construction made T-Series feel this was a particularly good time to attempt it. That possibility seems far more ordinary to me than either political conspiracy theory.

Then comes the director.

Om Raut had won significant recognition for Tanhaji, a large-scale historical film. On paper, I can understand why producers might have believed he could handle an epic project.

Once they decided to mount Ramayana at a huge scale, the budget naturally became enormous. To recover that investment, they needed a face with pan-India theatrical pull.

After Baahubali, choosing Prabhas as that face was commercially understandable — even if, in hindsight, whether he was the perfect fit for this particular role is a completely different question.

So far, so good.

For me, the major failure was the execution.

The team could not handle the level of CGI required convincingly, and they also seemed caught between faithfully retelling an epic and trying to redesign it for a modern audience that will question every creative shortcut.

They ultimately created their own heavily altered visual and tonal version of Ramayana — and many of those choices backfired badly.

That explanation may sound boring compared with a giant political conspiracy... but sometimes a badly planned and badly executed film is simply that.

And who am I to say all this?

I am neither here as a political devotee nor as a political hater. I am neither deeply religious nor an atheist. I am neither a hardcore Prabhas fan nor someone waiting to attack him.

I have loved and hated movies from every industry based primarily on what I experienced on screen, not on whatever political intent strangers online assign to them 😊

I am just an APOLITICAL MOVIE BUFF!!!!
rating_context: Rating reflects the author’s stated opinion of Adipurush, not the editorial article itself.
